title: Policy Composer for Multi-Objective SLA Smoothing and Safety
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated fleets currently use single-metric scaling triggers (primarily RPS or average latency) which leads to oscillation under bursty workloads and poor tail latency during tenant spikes. We need a policy composer that accepts multiple target metrics (latency quantiles, token throughput, error budget consumption), composes them into a stable scaling objective, and enforces safety limits (rate-of-change, min/max capacity, cost guardrails).

Scope: Design and implement an autoscaling policy engine component that: 1) exposes a declarative policy DSL for combining targets (e.g., p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, 429/error-rate), 2) supports multiple scaling algorithms (PID-like smoother, gradient-limited stepper, short-term predictive model using simple EWMA forecasts), 3) enforces safety constraints (max delta-per-minute, tenant-level cost cap, fleet-wide reserve headroom), 4) integrates with existing scheduler/orchestrator and telemetry pipelines, and 5) provides observability and dry-run mode for rollout.

Target metrics and composition examples: - Primary objective: p99 latency <= 250ms for routes configured with low-latency SLA. - Secondary objective: sustained tokens/sec >= configured throughput (per-tenant). - Safety objective: error rate (5xx+429) < 0.5% and cost delta < weekly budget threshold. - Composition semantics: weighted lexicographic comparator where latency quantile violations are prioritized over throughput once error budget exceeds threshold.

Scaling algorithms proposed: - Smoother (low-latency SLO mode): a PID-derived controller with derivative dampening and integral wind-down to avoid overshoot on long tails. - Stepper (cost-conservative mode): discrete step increases with cooling_period and exponential backoff on failures. - Predictive burst buffer: short-window EWMA forecast of tokens/sec + spike detector to pre-warm a small burst pool. - Emergency vent: immediate temporary capacity grant that is strictly bounded by safety caps and requires a cooldown and automated rollback.

Safety limits and guardrails: - min_capacity_per_tenant and max_capacity_per_tenant enforced at evaluator time. - max_scale_rate: limit on replicas or GPU units per minute to prevent noisy neighbor incidents. - cost_cap_label: stop-growth action when predicted cost delta breaches tenant cap (with notification path to SRE). - automatic rollback window: after emergency vent, return to previous capacity within X minutes unless SLO still violated.

Interfaces and runtime integration: - New Policy CRD-like JSON model persisted in config store and surfaced in Console. - Policy engine runs as sidecar service in orchestration plane and emits decisions as proposed actions (dry-run vs apply). - Decision payload includes rationale: contributing metrics, weights, confidence (from EWMA variance). - Integrate with tracing and existing per-route dashboards for auditability.

Observability and testing: - Expose decision logs, proposed vs applied, and a policy simulator endpoint to run historic traces. - Add eval harness scenarios (steady state, ramp, sustained burst, spike+drop) and SLO regression tests. - Dashboard panels for policy health: frequency of emergency vents, average scale delta, and overshoot incidence.

Rollout plan: 1) implement policy composer library + unit tests (2 weeks), 2) integrate EWMA predictor + simulator (1 week), 3) internal dry-run on low-risk fleet with Console visibility (2 weeks), 4) staged rollout by tenant tiers with monitoring alarms + manual kill switch (2 weeks), 5) enable for general Dedicated customers behind opt-in flag.

Dependencies: relies on improved telemetry ingestion (ENG-97321), updated quota/cost API (ENG-17645), and Console rollout UI (PM-440).

Acceptance criteria: - Policies can be declared and persisted via API and edited in Console. - Engine produces correct decisions in simulator for four canonical scenarios. - No regression in platform-wide P99 for canary tenants after 2 weeks. - Safety limits prevented any tenant from increasing capacity faster than max_scale_rate in chaos tests.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Patel: Initial RFC posted. Added concrete composition semantics and emergency vent concept. Requested feedback from SRE and product on cost cap behavior.
2026-03-04 - Maria Gonzales (SRE): Safety caps look reasonable. Need explicit backpressure path from scheduler when nodes are constrained — added ENG-70421 as dependent ticket.

2026-03-06 - Liam O'Connor: Prototype of PID-derived smoother checked into feature branch (pr: github.com/redwood/infra/pulls/932). Early tests show reduced oscillation but slower recovery for sustained 10x bursts — adding predictive burst buffer to handle that.

2026-03-09 - Sofia Martinez (Product): Prioritize low-latency route policies for enterprise customers; recommend default weight for p99=0.7, tokens/sec=0.2, error_budget=0.1. Also asked for Console UX mockups (design: DES-2198).

2026-03-11 - Liam O'Connor: Dry-run telemetry pipeline ready. Running simulation against last quarter's production traces. Observed one regression case when cost_cap activated too early; tuning cost prediction window to 30m fixed false positives.
